statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{X}$ be an algebraic stack over $S$.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is a stack in setoids and
$\mathcal{X} \to (\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is limit preserving on objects,
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is a stack in setoids and limit preserving,
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is representable by an algebraic space
locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}

semantic_review_note: The lemma states equivalence of exactly three conditions on an algebraic stack over S: stack in setoids plus limit preservation on objects; stack in setoids plus full limit preservation; and representability by an algebraic space locally of finite presentation. All three alternatives, the setoid qualifications on the first two, and locally finite presentation on the third survive. The section distinguishes limit preservation on objects from full limit preservation.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-diagonal}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a category fibred
in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Assume
$\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$ is
representable by algebraic spaces and $\mathcal{X}$ is limit preserving.
Then $\Delta$ is locally of finite type.
